course_title: Tools and Techniques for Business Analysis
course_description:
What makes a ‘good’ business decision? In this course, you will apply various rational and alternative tools to analyse real-world cases to explore how decisions are made and how they can be improved. By questioning perspectives, assumptions, and values, you will practice critical thinking as the most important employability skill for you to make strategic, evidence-based decisions in a complex and ambiguous world.

Course Changes in Response to Previous Student Feedback

In response to student uncertainty about the requirement to complete a site visit prior to the boardroom role plays, a separate due date has been created for this piece of assessment. To improve student confidence going into the boardroom role play, team formation processes will be strengthened and students will have opportunities to practice before the assessments.

restrictions: Students in the MBus(24 unit) program are not permitted to enrol in this course.

course_aims: This course aims to develop your critical thinking and decision-making skills by evaluating various tools and diverse perspectives. You will learn to analyse case studies, recognise complexity, make evidence-based, responsible decisions, and justify your arguments.

learning_outcomes.description: Analyse real-world business problems using relevant analytical tools.
Collaboratively evaluate business decisions from different perspectives.
Recommend strategies to balance the needs of shareholders and other stakeholders.
Justify positions supported by evidence and respect for the audience.
Reflect on personal assumptions and values to question business norms and challenge the status quo.

assessment_details.title: Boardroom Roleplay
assessment_details.due_date: Boardroom Roleplay 1 Boardroom Roleplay 2 Boardroom Roleplay 3 In-person during allocated workshops.
assessment_details.other_conditions: Time limited, Peer assessed, Secure. See the conditions definitions
assessment_details.task_description: Students will have three opportunities to engage in a boardroom roleplay in their allocated tutorial with their team. These assessed tutorials will be held in Weeks 7, 8, and 9 with the best two (2) marks of the three (3) submissions contributing to their grade. The boardroom roleplay is worth 15 marks, totalling 30 marks (2 x 15 marks). This is a secure assessment and no devices are allowed. Students must bring a pen and may bring one page of notes, a printed copy of the case study and a printed copy of the lecture slides to the tutorial. Teams are expected to provide peer evaluation data at the end of each of these three tutorials. While this is a team-based task, adjustments may be made to individual student marks based on the quality of their individual section and/or their performance within the boardroom roleplay. These adjustments may be made on the basis of peer evaluation data and/or teaching team observations. Read full task description Hide full task description

assessment_details.title: Business Tools For Making Decisions
assessment_details.task_description: Students will be provided t hree in-class reflective tasks that will inform the development of a 5-minute video submission. Each reflective task will be discussed and developed in the final workshops of the course and will draw upon course concepts and themes and student's own personal experience. These reflections should be synthesised and distilled into a 5-minute business leadership manifesto that should be recorded as a video and demonstrate professional communication. This video should be addressed to the student's future self and outline what kind of business leader the student would like to be. Read full task description Hide full task description
